question_text: A 45-year-old man with type 1 diabetes mellitus comes to the physician for a health maintenance examination. He has a 10-month history of tingling of his feet at night and has had two recent falls. Three years ago, he underwent retinal laser photocoagulation in both eyes. Current medications include insulin and lisinopril, but he admits not adhering to his insulin regimen. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. His blood pressure is 130/85 mm Hg while sitting and 118/70 mm Hg while standing. Examination shows decreased sense of vibration and proprioception in his toes and ankles bilaterally. His serum hemoglobin A1C is 10.1%. Urine dipstick shows 2+ protein. Which of the following additional findings is most likely in this patient?
